decision: phone exploration blocked: the test phone is offline, so research and scaffold first and explore FitNotes when it returns
why: the user asked to explore first, but nothing else depends on the phone being up

decision: Flutter for Android, package de.schurr.setlist, repo setlist, local SQLite only
why: Flutter is the owner's default app stack and the build server already builds Flutter APKs; Flutter compiles to a native Android app

decision: package:sqlite3 (synchronous, bundled via build hooks) instead of sqflite
why: one API for the app, for VPS tests, and for reading a FitNotes backup, which is itself a SQLite file

decision: wrote the product contract and the done predicate before any code
why: the arena runners and the implementer need one contract to build against

decision: docked editing panel at the bottom plus a full-day list above, instead of editing inside each row
why: big inputs stay in one thumb-reach place, the keyboard never covers the list, and it matches the FitNotes stepper habit

decision: cascade by equality: an edit updates later planned sets that still hold the old value
why: one tap progresses straight sets while warm-up and back-off sets keep their own values

decision: ran an arena of two independent design sketches for domain, persistence and screen state
why: the SQLite schema will hold years of his history, so it is worth designing twice

decision: kept equality cascade over Motra's delta cascade (shift every later unlogged set by the same amount)
why: delta would also shift working sets when a warm-up is edited; equality covers straight sets, the common case after a copy

decision: exercise kind becomes a table of FitNotes' ten measure combinations (weight, reps, time, distance) instead of three kinds
why: the import must not lose cardio or timed sets, and one table drives which steppers the panel shows

decision: rest timer posts an ongoing countdown notification and an exact alarm that vibrates at the end
why: a Dart timer stops firing once the screen is off and the CPU sleeps; competitors use a notification for the same reason

decision: import FitNotes sets in _id order, exercise order by smallest set _id, weight from metric_weight as kg, distance converted from training_log.unit
why: these are the conventions in the decompiled FitNotes source and two working importers

decision: skip routines and supersets in v1, report their counts after import
why: copying a past day covers the owner's workflow; the importer says what it left out instead of hiding it

decision: verified the bundled SQLite runs on the phone before building on it
why: riskiest unknown in the stack, so it went first
evidence: probe APK on the Nord rendered 'sqlite 3.53.4'

decision: reproduced all four pain points in FitNotes 25.1 on the phone, then unticked the sets I had ticked
why: the user asked for hands-on exploration first; his test-phone data stays as it was

decision: took a FitNotes backup on the phone and pulled it to the scratch folder as the importer's real test file

evidence: local scratch folder, findings in docs/fitnotes-notes.md

decision: keep the screen on while the app is open
why: the owner uses Keep Screen On in FitNotes

decision: import treats every set on a past day as done and uses is_complete only for today and later
why: past copied placeholders were never ticked, yet FitNotes counts all logged rows in history

decision: add a note per set
why: FitNotes keeps comments per set and an import must keep them

decision: importer takes weight step and rest time from FitNotes, treating NULL and 0 as the FitNotes global defaults

decision: picked candidate 1 as the base design; the judge agreed (C1 scored 20 of 25, C2 18)
